{{Short description|Danish geophysicist (1944–2018)}}
'''Eigil Friis-Christensen''' (29 October 1944 – 21 September 2018)<ref>[http://www.iaga-aiga.org/news/eigil-friis-christensen-passed-away/ Eigil Friis-Christensen passed away]</ref> was a Danish [[geophysics|geophysicist]] specializing in [[space physics]].

== Career ==

Friis-Christensen received a Magisterkonferens (Ph.D. equivalent) in [[Geophysics]] from [[University of Copenhagen]] in 1971.<ref name="correlations">{{cite web|url=http://www.ntva.no/Arrangement/seminar/cv/friis.htm |title=Correlations between Solar Activity and Global Climate |accessdate=2008-04-23 |publisher=ntva.no |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070814040214/http://www.ntva.no/Arrangement/seminar/cv/friis.htm |archivedate=2007-08-14 }}</ref> In 1972, he was a geophysicist at the Danish Meteorological Institute.  His interest in solar activity began in August, in his tent, when he experienced an extreme solar storm:<ref name="national">{{cite news|first=Lawrence |last=Solomon |title=Science, not politics |url=https://nationalpost.com/news/story.html?id=5b824408-9df0-4189-86fc-cf6465bf0aa8 |newspaper=National Post |date=2007-04-13 |accessdate=2008-04-23 }}{{dead link|date=October 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>
<blockquote>
"I was in Greenland, on my first assignment in my new job as geophysicist at the Danish Meteorological Institute, setting up a chain of magnetometer stations on the west coast... watching ink pens of my recorder going so wild that they nearly tore the paper chart apart -- we had no digital recording at that time -- and I wondered whether such big events could also have an influence in the lower atmosphere, on weather and climate. That storm cut off my contact to the outside world for nine days -- all radio communication was blacked out -- so I had lots of time to reflect on the enormity of the forces at play." 
</blockquote>

Between 1976 and 1997, he was the [[Principal investigator|Principal Investigator]] of the [[Greenland]] [[Magnetometer]] Array.

Between 1991 and 1997, he was Head of the Solar-Terrestrial Physics Division, [[Danish Meteorological Institute]]. In 1992, he was also the Project scientist on the first Danish satellite, [[Ørsted (satellite)|Ørsted]], which was launched February 1999.

He was an adjunct professor of geophysics and space physics 1996 to 2006 <ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dnva.no/c27368/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27375 |title=Professor Dr. Eigil Friis-Christensen, Danish National Space Center, DTU |accessdate=2008-04-23 |publisher=dnva.no |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110521013601/http://www.dnva.no/c27368/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27375 |archive-date=2011-05-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref> at the [[Niels Bohr Institute]] of [[University of Copenhagen]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.isac-esa.org/CVEigil%20Friis-Christensen.htm |title=CV - Eigil Friis-Christensen |accessdate=2008-04-23 |publisher=isac-esa.org |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070926234537/http://www.isac-esa.org/CVEigil%20Friis-Christensen.htm |archivedate=2007-09-26 }}</ref> and has authored over 140 research articles or books.<ref name="birkeland"/> He lectures worldwide;<ref name="correlations"/> in 2008 he made a presentation at the U.S. National Institute of Aerospace.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nianet.org/seminarscolloquia/2008/friis_022808.php |title=Solar Activity Variations, Cosmic Rays, Clouds, and Climate Change |accessdate=2008-04-23 |date=2008-02-28 |publisher=nianet.org |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080509071013/http://www.nianet.org/seminarscolloquia/2008/friis_022808.php |archivedate=May 9, 2008 }}</ref>

From 2004 until 2012 Friis-Christensen was Director of the [[Danish National Space Center]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.space.dtu.dk/Om_dtuspace/Historisk_baggrund | title=Historisk baggrund for instituttet | publisher=Danmarks Tekniske Universitet, DTU Space | date=2016-03-04 | accessdate=2016-10-03 | quote=Kristian Pedersen efterfølger Eigil Friis-Christensen, der var direktør for Danmarks Rumcenter og sidenhen DTU Space fra 2004 og frem til 2012.}}</ref>

== Solar activity and climate change ==
Friis-Christensen's 1991 paper, "Length of the Solar Cycle: An Indicator of Solar Activity Closely Associated with Climate", published in ''Science'',<ref>{{Cite journal |author1=Friis-Christensen, E. |author2= Lassen, K. |name-list-style=amp |date=1991-11-01 |issue= 5032|pages= 698–700 |doi=10.1126/science.254.5032.698 |title=Length of the Solar Cycle: An Indicator of Solar Activity Closely Associated with Climate |journal=Science |volume=254 |pmid=17774798 |s2cid= 31048860 }}</ref> presented his findings on global warming and sun activity correlation.<ref name="national"/> ''The New York Times'' reviewed the ''Science'' article on 5 November 1991, stating, "While the correlation established by Dr. Friis-Christensen and Dr. Lassen falls short of definite proof, a number of scientists nevertheless called it remarkable in its close fit between the solar and temperature trends."<ref>{{cite news |first=William K. |last=Stevens |title=Danes Link Sunspot Intensity to Global Temperature Rise |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1991/11/05/news/danes-link-sunspot-intensity-to-global-temperature-rise.html |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=1991-11-05 |access-date=2008-04-23}}</ref> Subsequent work with updated data has found that the correlation has not stood up and revealed that it was due to artifacts of the methodology used by Friis-Christensen.<ref name=DamonLaut04>{{cite journal|last=Damon|first=P.E.|author2=P. Laut|title=Pattern of strange errors plagues solar activity and terrestrial climatic data|journal=EOS|year=2004|volume=85|issue=39|pages=370, 374|doi=10.1029/2004eo390005|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Chatzistergos |first=Theodosios |date=2022-12-27 |title=Is there a link between the length of the solar cycle and Earth's temperature? |journal=Rendiconti Lincei. Scienze Fisiche e Naturali |language=en |doi=10.1007/s12210-022-01127-z |s2cid=255207798 |issn=2037-4631|doi-access=free }}</ref>

In 1997, Friis-Christensen and [[Henrik Svensmark]] revived suggestions of a possible link between [[galactic cosmic rays]] and [[global climate change]] assisted by [[solar wind]] intensity variation, which they termed [[cosmoclimatology]]. In 2002, he became Lead Investigator of [[Swarm (spacecraft)|Swarm]]. Friis-Christensen gave the [[Kristian Birkeland|Birkeland]] lecture "Unrest on the sun - storms on the Earth. The magnetic connection" in [[Oslo]] on  27 September 2007 .<ref name="birkeland">{{cite web |url=http://www.dnva.no/binfil/download.php?tid=27269 |title=The Birkeland Lecture 2007 |accessdate=2008-04-23 |last=Astad |first=Anne-Marie |publisher=knva.no |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110521013506/http://www.dnva.no/binfil/download.php?tid=27269 |archive-date=2011-05-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2009, a number of leading experts, including one Nobel laureate, concluded that the graphs of Friis-Christensen and Svensmark showing apparent correlations between global warming, sunspots and cosmic rays were deeply flawed.  Friis-Christensen agreed that any correlation between sunspots and global warming that he may have identified in the 1991 study has since broken down. There is, he said, a clear "divergence" between the sunspots and global temperatures after 1986, which shows that the present warming period cannot be explained by solar activity alone.<ref>{{cite news|title=Sun sets on sceptics' case against climate change |date=December 14, 2009 |author=Steve Connor |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/environment/climate-change/sun-sets-on-sceptics-case-against-climate-change-1839875.html }}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
* 1995, "Director Ib Henriksens" research prize.
* 1995, elected member, executive committee, International Association of [[Geomagnetism]] and [[Aeronomy]], IAGA. 
* 1996, elected Associate of London's [[Royal Astronomical Society]]
* 2003, Vice-President, executive committee, IAGA
* Appointed member, International Steering Committee, Solar-Terrestrial Energy Programme, STEP and S-RAMP.
* 2008, Foreign member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]]
